text:
alex: hey @it-ops — just finished laptop setup and VPN shows as connected, but I can't reach internal docs at https://intranet.redwood.internal. `curl` just times out. Using the WireGuard split-tunnel profile from the onboarding guide. anyone seen this? :confused:

it-ops: hi alex — most likely DNS for the internal zone isn't being pushed over split-tunnel. quick checks: 1) what does `scutil --dns` show? 2) `route -n get default` output? which VPN profile (newhire-prod vs newhire-dev)?

alex: output snippet:```
$ curl -v https://intranet.redwood.internal
*   Trying 10.10.2.12...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* connect to 10.10.2.12 port 443 failed: Operation timed out
* Failed to connect to intranet.redwood.internal port 443: Operation timed out
```
and `scutil --dns` shows no search domains for the VPN interface, only public DNS entries. I'm on `newhire-prod`.

maya: yup this is DNS. For split-tunnel we only push internal nameservers for the `*.redwood.internal` zone. On macOS the easiest fix is to create an /etc/resolver entry so the system knows to use the internal nameserver:```sudo sh -c 'echo "nameserver 10.10.0.53" > /etc/resolver/redwood.internal' && sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder```
That will force queries for that zone to the internal DNS. If you prefer a temporary test, try:```dig @10.10.0.53 intranet.redwood.internal +short```
If that returns an IP, DNS is the issue.

alex: tried to write `/etc/resolver/redwood.internal` but got `permission denied` when piping to the file (nevermind sudo didn't apply to the redirect).

jamie: I can run a one-liner for you via remote session or you can do:```echo 'nameserver 10.10.0.53' | sudo tee /etc/resolver/redwood.internal >/dev/null && sudo killall -HUP mDNSResponder```
Also make sure you have the onboarded SSH key for the bastion if you need to reach non-public services — onboarding doc is at https://docs.redwood.com/onboarding/internal-access (requires internal access). If the `dig` against 10.10.0.53 returns nothing, ping me and I'll open a ticket with infra.

alex: ran the `tee` command, then `curl` now returns HTML. :tada: thanks! feel free to push this into the new-hire checklist, tripped a bunch of folks on macs.

devex-bot: created ticket #INFR-3589 to add a macOS resolver step to the onboarding guide and to update the WireGuard profile notes.

jamie: noted, will follow up in the ticket and add a Jamf policy to ensure resolver is present for managed macs. :+1:
